title: How Nature Works in Harmony

standard_text: Ecosystems and their living and non-living parts; producers, consumers and decomposers; food chains and food webs; energy flow; interdependence, pollination and symbiosis; biodiversity, endangered and endemic species; conservation and protected areas in India (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 12).

key_big: Producers, consumers and decomposers depend on each other.

body_html:
How to think about it

An ecosystem is made of living things and their non-living surroundings. Producers (green plants and algae) make food using sunlight; herbivores eat them, carnivores eat other animals, and decomposers such as fungi and bacteria return nutrients to the soil. Linked food chains form a food web, and energy decreases at each step.

Living things depend on each other: bees pollinate flowers, lichens are a partnership of fungus and alga, and removing one species affects others. We protect biodiversity in national parks such as Jim Corbett and Kaziranga, through Project Tiger and biosphere reserves such as the Nilgiris.

Example

grass → ? → frog → snake

eats grass, eaten by frogs

Answer: grasshopper

Example

Mushroom: producer, consumer or decomposer?

feeds on dead matter

Answer: decomposer

Common mistakes

  • Starting a food chain with an animal.
  • Thinking decomposers are useless.
  • Thinking removing one species affects nothing.

faq.q: What is the role of decomposers?
faq.a: They break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil for producers to use.

faq.q: Why are food chains usually short?
faq.a: A lot of energy is lost at each step, so there is not enough left to support many levels.
